correctness.rationale: For m=n−1≥2, the published sign-vector adjacency model identifies the flip graph with P3^{□m} minus its center. Tensor-sum eigenvalues of P3 are 0,1,3, hence Kirchhoff gives T_m exactly. Weighted tree cofactor det(K+(t−1)D) has neighbor Green matrix M, invariant under signed permutations, with eigenvalue 1 on constants, m copies of α=E[1/(1+3Bin(m−1,2/3))] on opposite-sign contrasts and m−1 copies of β=(1−3^{−(m−1)})/[2(m−1)] on pair-symmetric contrasts; the supplied tensor-pseudoinverse derivation tracks the normalization. Thus degree pgf t(1−α+αt)^m(1−β+βt)^{m−1}. Leaf deletion gives coefficient [t]=2m τ(G_m), yielding the claimed exact tree count; limits follow mα→1/2,(m−1)β→1/2. Independently constructed exact weighted Kirchhoff cofactors for m=2,3 at enough distinct weights to check the full polynomial; this does not prove the general case.

value.rationale: The signohedron is a canonical polytope with a natural coherent monotone-path flip graph; its spanning-tree number measures global connectivity and normally entails an exponentially large determinant. An all-dimensional closed product and a striking full central UST-degree factorization into two binomials quantify removal of the forbidden center. The Poisson(1) limiting excess and e^(−1) tree-survival factor add interpretable asymptotic structure; this is a motivated exact graph invariant, not a known-table recomputation.
